reason: E1 demonstrates that coherent nanoprecipitates can enhance ductility in a W-based RHEA, but it describes a different alloy and a stepwise precipitation strategy, not the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy. E2 reports on Wx(TaVZr)100−x alloys and shows a multiphase microstructure with Laves and Zr-rich HCP phases, not coherent nanoprecipitates, and does not measure tensile ductility or toughness. Thus, the key premise that the equimolar alloy forms coherent, ductility-enhancing nanoprecipitates is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates form in equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy
These precipitates are Zr-enriched or related refractory nanoprecipitates
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations
This mechanism delays crack nucleation and enhances ductility/toughness
The effect is operative under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions (~800 °C)
